issues.problem: The suggestion virūkṣaṇī is right, but the metre argument is false: ru stands before the conjunct kṣ, so it is heavy by position whatever the vowel length. The metre does not decide the reading; the long ū comes from vi-√rūkṣ alone.
issues.fix: why: 'The word is from vi-√rūkṣ with long ū (virūkṣaṇa); the Devanagari also has short उ (विरुक्षणी). The metre does not decide it (ru is heavy by position before kṣ). Probable typo.'

issues.problem: The stem is viśva (n., dry ginger, = viśvabheṣaja), not viśvā: a feminine ā-stem would give -viśvābhiḥ, while the printed -viśvaiḥ needs an a-stem. viśvā (f.) is a different drug (usually ativiṣā). Same error in English, Hindi and notes.
विश्वा should be विश्व (stem viśva, n.).
Dry ginger is viśva (n.); viśvā (f.) names another drug.
